At the start of each discussion, stakeholders were provided with a project overview. Interviews were recorded and a set of summary notes was prepared from each interview. The questions for the focus groups were: 1. What are the main benefits of adaptive lighting technologies? 2. What do you think are the main organizational barriers to adoption and implementation? 3. What do you think are the main policy barriers to adoption and implementation? 4. Do you believe that adopting and implementing adaptive lighting technology is risky? If yes, how is this risk perceived? How is this risk alleviated? 5. Was there a key individual who championed the adoption of adaptive lighting? If yes, why was this person so crucial and would the technology have been adopted without them? 6. Was there any resistance to the adoption of adaptive lighting technology? If yes, what are they? How were they alleviated? 7. Did successful adoption necessitate the creation of new organizational roles? If yes, what were these roles? 8. Were there road and residential user acceptability issues in relation to adaptive lighting technology? If yes, what were these and how were these overcome? 9. Did you take any steps to address the users before adopting this technology? 10. Was the city encouraged by the manufacturers of adaptive lighting technology to adopt? If yes, how was this manifested? 11. Was the city well supported by the manufacturers of adaptive lighting technology? If yes, what form did this support take? If no, what problems did this create? 12. How has your engagement with the electric utility assisted in the adoption and implementation of adaptive lighting technology? 13. Do you believe that there would have been adoption without the electric utility’s support? 14. Is your engagement with the electric utility still ongoing? If yes, what form does this take? 50 15. Is there a “How to Why to” guide for adopting adaptive lighting technology? 16. Will this “How to Why to” guide be of any relevance to you? Or do you think that your adoption process can now be considered complete? 17. Do you believe that the difficulties in trust experienced in adopting adaptive lighting technology are specific or would they apply to other technologies like Smart city technologies? 18. Do you think that best practice can be prescribed for adaptive lighting technology adoption? If yes, can you indicate what form this would take? 19. Reflecting on the adoption and implementation process for adaptive lighting technology, if you were to undertake this process again what would you do differently and why? 4.1.5 Public Assessment A survey was developed to evaluate the opinion of the public. The purpose of this survey was to understand the influence of adaptive lighting on perceptions of safety, security, and energy efficiency from the standpoint of the general population in a city or town.
